note — the bold part is what the card te: warten auf + accusative: auf den Bus. English for, German auf.
denken an + accusative: to think of.

English: Are you thinking of **the appointment**? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: an + accusative: den Termin. Denk an…! also means don't forget.
sich freuen auf: glad about something still to come.

English: The children are looking forward to **the holidays**.
German: Die Kinder freuen sich auf **die Ferien**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: auf die Ferien: still to come.
sich freuen über: glad about something already here.
sich erinnern an + accusative: to remember.

English: He dreams of **a house** by the sea.
German: Er träumt von **einem Haus** am Meer.
note — the bold part is what the card te: träumen von: von always takes the dative.

English: Are you afraid of **the dog**? (one friend)

note — the bold part is what the card te: aufpassen auf + accusative: the prefix auf goes last, after the object.
For a thing, ask with wo + the preposition: worauf. An r joins them before a vowel.
For a person, keep the preposition and use wen: auf wen.

English: **What** are you looking forward to? (one friend)

note — the bold part is what the card te: für has no vowel to join, so no r: wofür.

English: The bus? I've been waiting **for it** for a long time.
German: Der Bus? Ich warte schon lange **darauf**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: For a thing, da + the preposition stands in for it: darauf = auf den Bus.

English: The exam? I'm not thinking **about it**.
The holidays? I'm looking forward **to them**.
The house by the sea? I dream **of it**.
German: Das Haus am Meer? Ich träume **davon**.

English: The holiday in Italy? I remember **it** well.
German: Der Urlaub in Italien? Ich erinnere mich gut **daran**.

English: The bill? Don't get annoyed **about it**! (one friend)
My grandma? I often think **of her**.
German: Meine Oma? Ich denke oft an **sie**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: For a person there is no da-: an + the pronoun, an sie.
